vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: social-media-autopilot-api
Version: 1.1.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate set of CLI tools for interacting with the SocialEcho social media management API. It uses native Node.js modules (http/https) without external dependencies, avoids risky practices by requiring explicit API key input via CLI arguments rather than environment variables, and contains no evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious execution logic. All scripts (e.g., client.js, publish-article.js) align with the functionality described in the SKILL.md and openapi.json files.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent CLI wrapper for the SocialEcho API: its files, README, and runtime behavior align with the described social-media management purpose and do not appear to perform unrelated or hidden actions.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match included files: CLI scripts, a client module, and OpenAPI specs for SocialEcho endpoints (team, account, article, report, upload URL, Reddit, Pinterest, publish). The code only implements requests to the declared API paths and local payload reading for publish; nothing requests unrelated services or credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the provided Node CLIs with explicit --api-key and optional --base-url/--team-id/--lang. The instructions avoid auto-reading env vars (explicitly), and the only local file access is reading a user-supplied JSON payload for publish. Note: allowing an arbitrary --base-url is useful for staging but means a provided API key could be pointed at any host if misused; that increases blast radius if an untrusted value is supplied.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only + code files). There are no external downloads or package installs declared; package.json has no runtime dependencies. This minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables and the SKILL.md instructs explicit CLI auth (--api-key). That is proportionate. Caveat: the CLI accepts --base-url which can be used to redirect requests (including the API key) to arbitrary hosts — a legitimate feature for testing but a potential data-leak vector if misused.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent or elevated platform privileges. always is false and there is no code modifying other skills or agent-wide configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a straightforward CLI client for the SocialEcho API. Before installing or running it: 1) Verify the source/author (registry metadata shows an opaque owner id and no homepage; _meta.json lists "socialecho-net") — if you expect an official client, confirm the publisher. 2) Keep your Team API key secret: run the tools in a trusted/isolated environment and pass the key only on the CLI (as the instructions say) or use ephemeral/limited keys where possible. 3) Do not supply an untrusted --base-url: that option will send your API key and data to whatever host you specify, so only use the default or a URL you control. 4) Review the included openapi.json/openapi.yaml and client.js (both are present) to ensure the behavior matches your expectations (the client uses GET with JSON bodies per the API design). 5) If you need higher assurance, test with a throwaway API key first and rotate keys after initial use.
